item.title: NBC TV to air Sheilla Yama’s Title-Retaining Bout tonight at 7:30 PM
item.description: The National Broadcasting Corporation (NBC) will broadcast a replay of Papua New Guinean boxer Sheilla Yama's latest title fight tonight at 7:30 pm on NBC TV. Yama, who hails from Mt Hagen, successfully defended her IBF International super lightweight title over the weekend in Auckland, New Zealand, defeating Australia's Jessica Messina on a unanimous points decision.
item.content:encoded:
The National Broadcasting Corporation (NBC) will broadcast a replay of Papua New Guinean boxer Sheilla Yama's latest title fight tonight at 7:30 pm on NBC TV.

Yama, who hails from Mt Hagen, successfully defended her IBF International super lightweight title over the weekend in Auckland, New Zealand, defeating Australia's Jessica Messina on a unanimous points decision.

The bout, held at Eventfinda Stadium on Auckland's North Shore, served as the main support fight on the Duco Events Ltd and Parker Promotions card.

The contest went the full ten-round distance for the first time in Yama's professional career, with judges scoring the fight in her favour across all three cards.

The win extends her unbeaten professional record to eight wins from eight fights, with three victories by stoppage.

Ranked No.2 in the world at her weight by the International Boxing Federation, Yama could next set her sights on a bout with either IBF No.1 contender Flora Pili of France or No.3 Hannah Robinson of England, with Ireland's Katie Taylor currently holding the IBF world title.

NBC is proud to bring this outstanding performance by one of Papua New Guinea's finest athletes to audiences nationwide.

Viewers are invited to tune in to NBC TV tonight at 7:30 pm to relive Yama's hard-fought victory.

item.title: Solar power project to be commissioned in Hela
item.description: A Solar Power Project at Yangome Village in Komo Hulia Electorate, Hela province is ready to be commissioned on 16th September 2026. The Yangome solar project in Hulia LLG is delivered by the Hela Provincial Government in partnership with Arafura Energies Ltd.
item.content:encoded:
A Solar Power Project at Yangome Village in Komo Hulia Electorate, Hela province is ready to be commissioned on 16th September 2026.

The Yangome solar project in Hulia LLG is delivered by the Hela Provincial Government in partnership with Arafura Energies Ltd.

It will run alongside two 2Mega Wats (MW) gas turbines already installed at Hides in partnership with ExxonMobil. Together, the 3MW of new generation is expected to end years of darkness for many Hela communities.

Hela governor, Philip Undialu said his people have lived for too long in darkness, without reliable power.

“On September 16th, we will switch on cheaper, reliable and sustainable electricity for Hela. This is our 50th Anniversary gift to our people," Undialu said.

Governor Undialu said the project aligns with the National Government’s broader policy to transfer the management of C-Centres to Provincial Governments and the private sector.

He said the model offers a practical solution to strengthen electricity services and ease pressure on the struggling PNG Power system.

"Through Hela Provincial Government and Arafura Energies Ltd, we are taking control of our energy future. This initiative will ensure our people, businesses, schools and health facilities have access to power that is affordable and dependable," he said.

Hela governor said the power rollout is about more than just lights. He said it will create new economic opportunities, support small businesses, improve service delivery in schools and hospitals, and lay the foundation for future industries in the province.

"For Hela, this is more than a power project. It is about opportunity. Hela will never be the same again," he said.

item.title: Border Command officers challenged to strengthen leadership
item.description: 27 Police officers from across the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary’s Border Command have been challenged to strengthen leadership and supervision within the force after completing a six-week Sergeant Course in Wewak. East Sepik Provincial Police Commander Christopher Tamari urged the newly qualified police officers to take their leadership responsibilities seriously and help address needs in m
item.content:encoded:
27 Police officers from across the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary’s Border Command have been challenged to strengthen leadership and supervision within the force after completing a six-week Sergeant Course in Wewak.

East Sepik Provincial Police Commander Christopher Tamari urged the newly qualified police officers to take their leadership responsibilities seriously and help address needs in middle management.

“For me, my take about these six weeks of training is you all are leaders. Go out there and help us, the PPCs and PSCs, to manage the middle management, which has been the problematic area in this great organisation, the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary,” PPC Tamari said.

He said the sergeants are a critical link between senior management and rank-and-file officers.

“You are the supervisors; you are the bridge between the top management and our rank and file,” he said.

PPC Tamari said the Border Command was serious about reform and expected the newly trained officers to contribute to that change.

“For us in Border Command, we are serious about change and becoming the shining light to other commands or directorates,” he said.

He challenged the officers to use their experience to find solutions to challenges they encounter in their respective areas of duty.

“Despite the challenges on the ground and that are forthcoming, you as the leaders are the solution. You are all very experienced and I trust you all to do your best,” PPC Tamari said.

The officers received Certificates of Attainment after graduating from course one of 2026 at the Village Inn Conference Room in Wewak on Friday 7th of August.

The graduation was attended by East Sepik caretaker provincial administrator Alphonse Kami and acting deputy provincial administrator for social services Emmanuel Tomarum.

Kami congratulated the graduating officers and reaffirmed East Sepik provincial government’s commitment to supporting policing and maintaining law and order in the province.

He said the provincial administration would continue working with police to strengthen policing services across East Sepik.

Meanwhile, PPC Tamari also acknowledged the families of the graduating officers for supporting them throughout the six-week training period.

item.title: Prime Minister Marape opens 2026 PNG investment conference in Brisbane
item.description: Prime Minister, James Marape has officially opened the 2026 Papua New Guinea Investment Conference on Monday, 10th August (today), in Brisbane, Australia. The two-day conference, organised by Business Advantage International, will be held at the Brisbane Convention and Exhibition Centre on August 10–11 and is expected to attract between 250 and 300 delegates, including senior business leaders, inv
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister, James Marape has officially opened the 2026 Papua New Guinea Investment Conference on Monday, 10th August (today), in Brisbane, Australia.

The two-day conference, organised by Business Advantage International, will be held at the Brisbane Convention and Exhibition Centre on August 10–11 and is expected to attract between 250 and 300 delegates, including senior business leaders, investors and representatives of development and industry organisations.

Now in its 14th year, the conference promotes investment and business opportunities across Papua New Guinea and provides an important platform for PNG businesses to engage with Australian and international investors.

Prime Minister Marape said his attendance reinforces the Government’s message that Papua New Guinea is open for business and welcomes stronger trade, investment and business partnerships with Australia and the wider international community.

“Papua New Guinea and Australia share a strong and enduring relationship.

“We want to continue strengthening the economic dimension of that relationship by encouraging greater investment, trade and business-to-business partnerships,” PM Marape said.

PM Marape said he would speak directly to investors about the country’s economy, progress of major resource projects and how the government is undertaking improvement on the business investment.

“We have enormous opportunities across mining, petroleum and LNG, agriculture, fisheries, forestry, tourism, infrastructure, financial services, construction and ICT, and we welcome genuine investors who want to partner with Papua New Guinea.” PM Marape said.

This year’s conference will also focus on artificial intelligence, human capital and skills development, while infrastructure development will be a major focus on the second day.

item.title: Nawaeb HQ to be reconnected after Busu bridge opening
item.description: Road access to the Nawaeb headquarters in Morobe is now open following the official commissioning of the new 72-metre Wenge-Brutten Bridge last Friday. The Bailey structure, built over the Busu River, will serve as a vital lifeline for the people of Boana and surrounding villages.
item.content:encoded:
Road access to the Nawaeb headquarters in Morobe is now open following the official commissioning of the new 72-metre Wenge-Brutten Bridge last Friday.

The Bailey structure, built over the Busu River, will serve as a vital lifeline for the people of Boana and surrounding villages.

This is the fourth bridge to be constructed at the location after the previous structure was washed away by floods in October 2023.

Outgoing Morobe administrator Max Brutten officiated at the opening and acknowledged the key leaders who contributed to funding and delivering the project.

Brutten recalled inspecting the damaged site shortly after the 2023 collapse and raising the urgency with former governor, the late Luther Wenge.

“I drove up here to see the bridge’s condition and was worried for the people of Boana,” Brutten said.

“I pushed the late governor to make sure reconstruction was prioritised.“

"Following that, the Morobe provincial government allocated K5 million from the Wafi-Golpu Infrastructure Development Grant, my administration put in another K5 million, and Governor Rainbo Paita approved K4.5 million to refurbish the road access leading to the bridge.”

Nawaeb district administrator Budz Botike welcomed the new bridge, but appealed for the main access road to the district headquarters to be sealed.

“Nawaeb contributes immensely to the country’s economy through high-quality coffee,” Botike said.

“It would be better if Governor Paita could follow up on our submissions to Waigani so our people can have proper road access.”

Morobe Governor Rainbo Paita assured local leaders that the provincial government would address the request.

“We will not wait for the National Government; we will move ahead to build our own roads,” Paita said.

“I direct our administrator and his team to identify funds under the Provincial Support Infrastructure Program to seal this road from the junction all the way to Boana headquarters.”

To honor the late former governor, Paita invited his son, Mathew Wenge, to cut the ribbon to officially open the bridge.

“Out of respect for our late governor, I ask my brother Mathew to perform the ribbon cutting,” Paita said.

The bridge was constructed over seven months by an Asian contractor and is engineered to last between 50 and 100 years.

item.title: National Cancer Team assesses SiPHA’s capacity
item.description: Simbu Provincial Health Authority (SiPHA) has hosted the National Cancer Control Program Team as part of the Highlands Regional Cancer Outreach from Monday 3rd to Thursday 6th August 2026. The team assessed SiPHA’s capacity to diagnose and manage cancer, and advocated for the new National Cancer Prevention and Control Strategic Plan 2025-2030.
item.content:encoded:
Simbu Provincial Health Authority (SiPHA) has hosted the National Cancer Control Program Team as part of the Highlands Regional Cancer Outreach from Monday 3rd to Thursday 6th August 2026.

The team assessed SiPHA’s capacity to diagnose and manage cancer, and advocated for the new National Cancer Prevention and Control Strategic Plan 2025-2030.

The visiting team comprised Manager of the National Cancer Program, George Otto, Chief Oncologist, Dr Manna Ario, Pediatric Oncologist, Dr Gwenda Anga, Adult Oncologist, Dr Aina Anota, and Admin Assistant, Anita Metofa.

SiPHA’s Director Curative, Dr Joseph Ande and Director Corporate Services, Henry Kua, together with Senior and Specialist Medical Officers, took the team on a tour of diagnostic and treatment services.

“We walked them through our Histopathology Laboratory, General Laboratory, Mammogram and CT/MRI services. We also showed them our Chemotherapy and Surgery units,” Dr Ande said.

He said the radiation component for Simbu patients is currently done at Angau Provincial Hospital in Lae, Morobe Province.

Dr Ande said SiPHA’s position is aligned to KRA 4 of the National Health Plan 2021-2030, SPA 3 of MTDP IV 2023-2027, and KPA 3 of SiPHA’s Corporate Plan 2025-2027.

“Our goal is to detect cancer early, treat as soon as possible, and increase awareness on preventative approaches so the cancer burden is reduced,” Dr Ande said.

He said the Marape-Rosso Government backed this vision in 2020 with K5 million in funding for cancer services.

Henry Kua, Director Corporate Services said the visit was important to identify gaps and strengthen partnerships.

“This outreach helps us see where we stand and what support we need from the National Department of Health to deliver better cancer care for Simbu people,” Mr Kua said.

National Cancer Program Manager, George Otto the said the Highlands outreach is part of a nationwide push.

“The new National Cancer Prevention and Control Strategic Plan 2025-2030 focuses on prevention, early detection, treatment and palliative care.

“We need all provinces to be ready,” Mr Otto said.

item.title: Simbu becomes 10th province to sign youth strategy plan
item.description: Simbu province has become the 10th province in the country to sign the Joint Inception and Implementation Plan under the National Youth Engagement Strategy 2025–2029, led by the National Youth Development Authority (NYDA). The initiative was launched in August 2025 under the Ministry of Youth, Religion and Community Development, as part of the Marape-Rosso Government’s target to create one million
item.content:encoded:
Simbu province has become the 10th province in the country to sign the Joint Inception and Implementation Plan under the National Youth Engagement Strategy 2025–2029, led by the National Youth Development Authority (NYDA).

The initiative was launched in August 2025 under the Ministry of Youth, Religion and Community Development, as part of the Marape-Rosso Government’s target to create one million jobs and opportunities for out-of-school and unemployed youth.

The program is guided by the theme “Putting Young People at the Center of Development.”

Director General of the National Youth Development Authority, Joe Itaki welcomed Simbu as the 10th province to formally adopt the strategy, calling it a major milestone for decentralized youth mobilization.

“Once Simbu’s youth are mobilized and registered through the new district-level databases, they will be directly slotted into agriculture, aquaculture, civil works, forestry, tourism, farming handicrafts, textile design and other areas of economic interest” Itaki said.

He said the joint implementation plans go beyond registration.

“We aim to establish formal District Youth Development Councils within the DDA structures. This ensures young citizens gain a legal legislative voice to influence local-level government decisions and participate directly in district planning,” he said.

Mr. Itaki added that NYDA is moving away from centralized city workshops.

“We are bringing the strategy straight into rural LLGs to capture school leavers and out-of-school young adults where they live.” he said.

Simbu Provincial Administrator, John Punde the said the program focuses on the group that will determine the future of the country.

“Preparing the next generation is always a challenge. But through such partnerships and programs we will be able to achieve positive outcomes,” Punde said.

He noted that because PNG is a rural-based country, reaching all citizens with government programs remains difficult.

“I commend the framework for using digital registration to connect young people with practical training and economic projects,” he added.

Mr. Punde also congratulated SinaSina Yongomugl district for being the first district in Simbu to pilot the project this year, and said he expects the other 5 districts in Simbu to join in from next year onwards.

Director of Hargy Oil Palms Limited, Robert Nilkare, gave strong support to the NYES 2025–2029, describing it as a practical framework to mobilize and prepare unemployed youth for the workforce.

“The immediate priority is to mobilize unemployed youth, systematically identify them, and build an organized database. Building this localized data resource is essential to successfully preparing young people for employment opportunities across all sectors in PNG,” Mr. Nilkare said.

He confirmed Hargy Oil Palms will be part of the drive by engaging youth in farms and plantations.

The NYDA socialisation program ran from 3rd to 6th August in Kundiawa with technical team presenting the insights and components of the new national framework to representatives from the province, district, NGO, Church and other stakeholders.

item.title: Madang police launch homicide investigation after body washes ashore in Bogia
item.description: The body of an adult male of Asian origin was found washed ashore at Sepa village in the Bogia district of Madang late yesterday afternoon, police say. Madang provincial police commander Supt Robert Baim confirmed last night that police officers and local district health workers were transporting the corpse to the Madang Town morgue.
item.content:encoded:
The body of an adult male of Asian origin was found washed ashore at Sepa village in the Bogia district of Madang late yesterday afternoon, police say.

Madang provincial police commander Supt Robert Baim confirmed last night that police officers and local district health workers were transporting the corpse to the Madang Town morgue.

“We are treating this as a murder case," Supt Baim said.

"I am calling on all fishing companies to check their crews, especially those of Asian origin, and report any missing persons from their vessels so we can properly identify the deceased."

Police suspect the deceased may have fallen off a fishing vessel or was deliberately thrown overboard.

Supt Baim said the body would be kept at the Modilon General Hospital morgue while police awaited reports from any vessel operating in PNG waters regarding missing crew.

He added that a post-mortem examination would be conducted to establish the exact cause of death.
